applies_to: GE Multilin PQMII power quality meters on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX ("lite" profile).
summary: Gateway profile for the GE PQMII: 531 objects (118 AI, 413 BI), 38 polled by default (currents, voltages, power, PF, demand and frequency). Hundreds of switch, relay, LED and alarm status bits and energy, harmonic and setup values are unpolled.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile GE_PQMII_Power_Meter_Lite_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the maker's Modbus register document (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/GEK-113532.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 38 of the 531 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.

integration.summary: Map 3-phase real power, 3-phase positive real energy and average line voltage first. The listed objects are read-only.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
